title: Winter sun from Newcastle in January: direct flights compared
author: Brogan
intro: January in the North East is cold and dark, but Newcastle has a good choice of direct flights to the sun, mostly with Jet2 and easyJet, plus Emirates to Dubai. Here's where you can fly in January, how long it takes and how warm each place usually is.
seo_title: Winter sun from Newcastle in January: 3 to 7 hrs away
seo_description: The Canaries are about 4½ hours from Newcastle and 20-22°C in January. Hurghada and Dubai are warmer but further. Every direct option compared.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Warm and close:** the Canaries, 4½ hrs
- **Warmest:** Dubai, about 24°C
- **New this winter:** easyJet to Hurghada
- **No jet lag:** the Canaries and Madeira

The temperatures are average January daytime highs from the climate figures in our guides. Flight times are typical direct times from Newcastle. We checked routes in November 2026 from airline and airport announcements, but timetables change, so check the airline's own schedule for your dates before you book.

For most people, it comes down to the Canaries for an easy week with no jet lag, or Hurghada and Dubai for something warmer and further away. Spain, Malta, Cyprus and Morocco are mild rather than hot in January, which suits sightseeing more than sunbathing.

sections.heading: The Canaries: the easy choice
sections.text:
Jet2 runs the biggest winter programme from Newcastle, and the four big Canary Islands are the heart of it. Tenerife alone has up to 11 Jet2 flights a week, and easyJet has added Fuerteventura this winter on Thursdays and Sundays.

- **[Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife) and [Gran Canaria](/destinations/gran-canaria):** the warmest islands in January, at about 22°C, with the sunniest resorts in the south.
- **[Lanzarote](/destinations/lanzarote):** calmer and a little cooler, with volcanic scenery and low white villages.
- **[Fuerteventura](/destinations/fuerteventura):** long, empty beaches, though it's often windy.

The Canaries are on UK time, so there's no jet lag even on a short trip. Our [Lanzarote or Fuerteventura](/blog/lanzarote-or-fuerteventura) and [Gran Canaria or Tenerife](/blog/gran-canaria-or-tenerife) posts help you choose an island.

sections.heading: Warmer and further: Hurghada and Dubai
sections.text:
If you want to be sure of warmth in January, go further:

- **[Hurghada](/destinations/hurghada):** new with easyJet from 27 October, on Tuesdays and Saturdays. It's about 21°C in January, with sunshine nearly every day and coral reefs offshore. UK visitors need a visa for Egypt, usually bought on arrival or online.
- **[Dubai](/destinations/dubai):** Emirates flies all year from Newcastle, in about seven hours. January is one of the best months, at about 24°C, and it's a good stopover for going further, to the Maldives or Thailand.

Watch out: Egypt is two hours ahead and Dubai four, so the flight home can feel long. Check GOV.UK's travel advice for each country before you book.

sections.heading: Mild city and coast breaks
sections.text:
Not every January trip needs beach weather. Jet2's flights to [Madeira](/destinations/madeira), [Málaga](/destinations/malaga), Faro, [Malta](/destinations/malta), [Paphos](/destinations/paphos) and [Marrakech](/destinations/marrakech) are good for a sunny few days of walking, sightseeing and long lunches outside, at around 16 to 19°C.

- **For walking:** Madeira's levada paths, at about 19°C.
- **For a city break:** Marrakech or Málaga, both sunny but with cool evenings.
- **For history:** Malta's old towns or the ancient sites around Paphos.

Tip: January is often the cheapest month of the winter once the New Year week is over. Look at the second and third weeks for the best prices on the Canaries.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Newcastle?
sections.text:
Start with [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife) or [Gran Canaria](/destinations/gran-canaria) for guaranteed warmth with no jet lag, or [Hurghada](/destinations/hurghada) for something new this winter. Our guide to [where you can fly direct from Newcastle](/blog/where-can-you-fly-direct-from-newcastle-airport) lists every route, and [how early to arrive at Newcastle Airport](/blog/how-early-should-you-arrive-at-newcastle-airport) covers the airport itself. For more ideas, see [where to go in January](/destinations/where-to-go-in-january).

If everyone wants somewhere different, add a few to somewhere.party, give everyone points to vote with, and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: Where is warmest in January with a direct flight from Newcastle?
faqs.answer: Dubai is the warmest, at about 24°C. Tenerife and Gran Canaria are about 22°C, with a much shorter flight and no time difference. Hurghada is about 21°C.

faqs.question: How long is the flight from Newcastle to Tenerife?
faqs.answer: About four and a half hours direct. Lanzarote and Fuerteventura are slightly shorter.

faqs.question: Does easyJet fly from Newcastle to Egypt?
faqs.answer: Yes. easyJet started flying from Newcastle to Hurghada on 27 October 2026, on Tuesdays and Saturdays. Check the current days on easyJet's timetable before you book.

faqs.question: Is Málaga warm in January?
faqs.answer: Málaga is mild rather than warm, at about 17°C by day. It's often sunny, which makes it good for a city break, but it's too cool for most people to swim.
